children: Noel Tata has written to the Tata Sons board for the second time, asking for the recording of the September 17 board meeting that reappointed N Chandrasekaran as chairman, people familiar with the matter told CNBC-TV18.
The letter, dated November 20, comes ahead of the Tata Sons board meeting scheduled for November 26.
What happened on September 17?

The Tata Sons board approved Chandrasekaran's third term by a 4-1 vote. Chandrasekaran did not vote. Noel Tata voted against the resolution, while Venu Srinivasan, the other Tata Trusts nominee on the board, voted in favour.
With the two Tata Trusts nominees split, the decision then went to Harish Manwani, chairman of the board's Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC), sources had told CNBC-TV18.
Why the meeting matters
Under Tata Sons' Articles of Association, key board decisions must also have the support of a majority of the Tata Trusts' nominee directors. Tata Trusts is the largest shareholder in Tata Sons.

Noel Tata argues that with one nominee voting each way, this majority was never reached and the resolution is invalid. Tata Sons says a 1-1 split among the nominees is a tie that a casting vote can break, and maintains the reappointment is legally valid.

A legal opinion from former Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud, obtained by Noel Tata, says a casting vote cannot create a majority where none exists. Noel Tata has also said he was not given enough time at the meeting to present this opinion.
The recording could show how the vote was conducted, and that is why Noel Tata keeps asking for it.
Tata Sons' earlier reply
Noel Tata first asked for the recording and the minutes in a letter dated September 30.

As CNBC-TV18 had reported, Tata Sons turned this down in a letter dated November 9. It said the September 17 meeting was held in person, and neither the law nor its Articles required it to keep or share audio-video recordings of such meetings with directors.

In the same letter, Tata Sons rejected his other concerns. It said it had reviewed his comments on the minutes and made the appropriate changes. It said Article 118, which provides for a selection committee to pick the chairman, does not apply when a sitting chairman is reappointed.
It also backed Srinivasan's vote, saying his association with TVS posed no conflict of interest, and said Tata Sons had no business dealings with TVS Motor or Hanno Warehousing.
What the new letter seeks

Noel Tata has now asked the board for detailed clarifications on the relationship between Hanno Warehousing and TVS Motor. Hanno Warehousing is run by Chandrasekaran's family. TVS Motor is the flagship company of the TVS Group, led by Srinivasan.
The letter also asks for details of the September 3 NRC meeting, including its recording. At that meeting, the committee decided to ask Chandrasekaran to reconsider his decision, the people said.
Trustee calls for restraint

Noel Tata's letter came a few hours after Bhaskar Bhat, a trustee of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT), urged fellow trustees to show restraint. Bhat raised concerns about Tata Group matters reaching the media and said this could hurt the Tata brand, which needed to be protected.
The Tata Sons board will meet on November 26.

title: Noel Tata writes to Tata Sons again, seeks recording of Chandrasekaran reappointment meeting
